Hi Marcel —

Thanks for sending these quickly and sorry for the friction. Short answer: we can usually accept one of the following paths to clear a PO when the IRS/US TIN lookup fails for non-US vendors:

- A notarized IRS 147-C letter or equivalent cert from the IRS confirming TIN (preferred), OR
- A bank letter (on bank letterhead, recent within 90 days) that shows the vendor legal name and IBAN/account details, PLUS a government business registry extract (translated to English if not already) showing legal name and registration number, OR
- For EU-registered entities, an apostilled business registry extract + KYC ID for the signer (passport or national ID) may suffice in lieu of 147-C.

Please use the DocuSign link below for the delegated-signatory acceptance so we have a signed acknowledgement for our records. I’ve flagged this PO as "on hold" in the procurement system until we have the final evidence. Once I have the registry extract I’ll loop payments.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/suites/12345-abcdef

If you can share the registry extract and a scanned KYC for the signatory we’ll try the EU-apostille route. If not, confirm and we’ll tell you whether the bank letter + registry extract path will be accepted by Payments.

Thanks,

Adding a quick procurement/payments checklist to be explicit on our side:

- Government business registry extract (official PDF) — English translation if original is not English. If EU: apostille recommended.
- Bank letter on bank letterhead, dated within last 90 days, with legal business name visible.
- Signed W-8BEN-E (you already provided) — matches legal entity name on registry extract.
- Scanned ID for the signatory who will sign any DocuSign (passport or national ID).
- If the vendor cannot get notarized 147c: include an official statement from your local tax authority or tax agent explaining how TIN verification is handled locally (helps Payments accept the alternative).

If all items above are provided we can set the PO to "Pending payment" and schedule release after a quick payments review (usually 3-5 business days).
